items.title: Complex structure on an associated bundle by realification
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group, let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth
right principal $H$-bundle, let $W$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, and let $\rho:H\to\mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W)$ be a smooth complex
representation. Regard $W$ as the underlying real vector space $W_{\mathbb R}$
and $\rho$ as the real representation $\rho_{\mathbb R}$. The associated
quotient $P\times_{H,\rho_{\mathbb R}}W_{\mathbb R}$ has the smooth real
vector-bundle structure supplied by the associated-vector-bundle theorem. The
map $J[p,w]=[p,iw]$ is well-defined and smooth and satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$.
It therefore gives this real bundle a complex vector-bundle structure of rank
$\dim_{\mathbb C}W$, with transition maps $\rho(g_{ji})$ in any local principal
trivializations $s_i=s_jg_{ji}$. This assertion specifies the complex structure
induced by $J$ and makes no uniqueness claim about other possible complex
structures on the same real bundle.

references.title: John M. Lee, Introduction to Smooth Manifolds, 2nd ed.
references.locator: §10, Lemma 10.6 (Vector Bundle Chart Lemma), PDF pp. 270–271: complete criterion and proof that fiberwise-linear local charts with smooth transition maps define a unique smooth real vector bundle. The complex structure on the realification is proved in this item.

items.physical_scope: Pure mathematical well-definedness result; it has no physical assumptions or empirical claim.

items.title: Rigid supersymmetric background and localization data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M$ be a nonempty Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, let $g$ be a smooth positive-definite metric on $TM$, and choose an orientation $o$. Coordinates $x^\mu$ have units of length, the metric components in length coordinates are dimensionless, and the scalar curvature has units of inverse length squared. A concrete background may instead have a boundary, but then its boundary conditions and the vanishing or treatment of every boundary term are additional data.

Write $SO(4)=\{R\in M_4(\mathbb R):R^{\mathsf T}R=I,\ \det R=1\}$. For $x\in M$, an oriented $g$-orthonormal frame is an orientation-preserving linear isometry $e:\mathbb R^4\to T_xM$. The oriented orthonormal frame bundle $F_g^+(M)$ is the set of these frames, with projection to $M$ and right action $e\cdot R=e\circ R$. Its smooth principal $SO(4)$-bundle structure is part of the supplied geometry. Use $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$, where $SU(2)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}:z,w\in\mathbb C,\ |z|^2+|w|^2=1\right\}$ and the two factors act by their defining matrix representations on $\mathbb C^2$. Identify each factor with the unit quaternions by $\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}\leftrightarrow z+w\mathbf j$, with $\mathbf j^2=-1$ and $\mathbf j z=\bar z\mathbf j$; write $\mathbb H=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,i,\mathbf j,i\mathbf j\}\cong\mathbb R^4$. The fixed standard double-covering homomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$ is $\rho(u_+,u_-)q=u_+qu_-^{-1}$; it is surjective with kernel $\{(1,1),(-1,-1)\}$. A Euclidean spin structure is a smooth right principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $\widetilde F\to M$ and a smooth map $\lambda:\widetilde F\to F_g^+(M)$ satisfying $\lambda(\widetilde p s)=\lambda(\widetilde p)\rho(s)$ for all $\widetilde p\in\widetilde F$ and $s\in\operatorname{Spin}(4)$, whose restriction to every fibre is a two-sheeted cover. The chiral spinor bundles are the associated bundles $S_\pm=\widetilde F\times_{\pi_\pm}\mathbb C^2$, where $\pi_\pm$ are the defining representations of the two $SU(2)$ factors and the quotient convention is $(ps,z)\sim(p,\pi_\pm(s)z)$. Equip each real associated bundle with the complex structure $[p,z]\mapsto[p,iz]$, so $S_\pm$ has complex rank two. A spin connection is a principal connection on $\widetilde F$ projecting to the Levi-Civita connection of $g$; it induces covariant derivatives on $S_\pm$. A spin structure and its connection are supplied data, not conclusions that follow from the metric.

An R-symmetry background consists of a specified finite-dimensional Lie group $K_R$, a smooth right principal $K_R$-bundle $P_R\to M$, a principal connection $A_R$, and a declared smooth representation of $K_R$ on each field bundle. Gauge data consist of a specified compact Lie group $G$, a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $P_G\to M$, its gauge group of smooth bundle automorphisms over $\operatorname{id}_M$, and a principal connection $A$. Matter and auxiliary fields are smooth sections of explicitly declared vector bundles associated to $\widetilde F$, $P_R$, and $P_G$; bosonic and fermionic fields are assigned even and odd parity, respectively. The curvature, global form of $G$, representations, bundle sectors, and reality contours are part of the model data.

For a spinor that carries an R-symmetry representation, let $U$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and declare its smooth representation $\varrho:K_R\to\mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb C}(U)$ and its chiral spin representation $\pi_\pm:\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to\mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb C^2)$. The smooth product principal $(\operatorname{Spin}(4)\times K_R)$-bundle $\widetilde F\times_M P_R$ has right action $(\widetilde p,p_R)\cdot(s,k)=(\widetilde p s,p_Rk)$; its local charts are products of the spin and R charts, and its product connection is the pair of the supplied principal connections. Use the product representation $(s,k)\mapsto\pi_\pm(s)\otimes\varrho(k)$; the associated spinor/R bundle uses the quotient convention $[(\widetilde p s,p_Rk),z]=[(\widetilde p,p_R),(\pi_\pm(s)\otimes\varrho(k))z]$. In simultaneous local sections $(\widetilde s_i,r_i)$, let $A_i^S=\widetilde s_i^*\omega^S$ and $A_i^R=r_i^*A_R$ be the local forms of the supplied spin and R connections. The associated-covariant-derivative definition gives, for a section with local component $\epsilon_i:U_i\to\mathbb C^2\otimes U$,
$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon_i=\partial_\mu\epsilon_i+\left((d\pi_\pm)_e(A^S_{i,\mu})\otimes I_U+I_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes(d\varrho)_e(A^R_{i,\mu})\right)\epsilon_i.$$
The displayed sum is the differential of the product representation, since differentiating $\pi_\pm(\exp(tX))\otimes\varrho(\exp(tY))$ at $t=0$ gives $(d\pi_\pm)_e(X)\otimes I_U+I_{\mathbb C^2}\otimes(d\varrho)_e(Y)$. Here each differential is taken at the identity of its group. This is the local expression of the connection induced by the product principal connection and representation; for an R-neutral spinor, $\varrho$ is the trivial representation. The mathematical supplier states this formula for a smooth finite-dimensional complex representation of a finite-dimensional Lie group and proves the local expressions patch; the current associated-covariant-derivative supplier is draft and its proof has not yet received independent acceptance. In $\mathscr K(\nabla^S,A_R,\mathcal B)(\epsilon)$, $\nabla^S$ and $A_R$ therefore act with these declared representations and conventions, not by an unspecified ordinary derivative.

A rigid supersymmetric background datum is a fixed Riemannian metric, spin structure and spin connection, R-symmetry background, supergravity auxiliary background fields, and a nonzero smooth spinor section $\epsilon$ in a declared spinor/R-symmetry representation. It also supplies the exact first-order linear system $\mathscr K(\nabla^S,A_R,\mathcal B)(\epsilon)=0$ imposed on $\epsilon$, where $\mathcal B$ denotes the named auxiliary background fields and $\mathscr K$ is the operator obtained by setting the chosen supergravity fermion variation to zero. The equation, its signature, gamma-matrix convention, spinor reality conditions, and boundary conditions must be specified separately for each model; no universal Killing-spinor equation or existence statement is built into this definition. “Rigid” means the metric and supergravity fields are fixed external data and are not integrated over.

An off-shell multiplet is a specified $\mathbb Z_2$-graded collection of bosonic, fermionic, and auxiliary fields together with an odd transformation $Q$ on all of them. An isometry is a diffeomorphism preserving $g$ and $o$; its action on associated bundles must also be supplied. A flavor transformation is the action of a separately named global internal group on the declared field representations. The multiplet closes off shell when $Q^2$ equals an explicitly declared combination of lifted spacetime isometries, gauge transformations, R-symmetry transformations, and flavor transformations on every field, without using Euler–Lagrange equations. A localization package additionally specifies its graded field configuration space $\mathcal F$, action $S$, and gauge group $\mathcal G$. The ordinary even configuration space $\mathcal F_{\bar0}$ and $\mathcal G$ carry supplied differentiable charts modeled on specified real Fréchet spaces: complete metrizable locally convex vector spaces with topology given by declared countable families of seminorms. For smooth section coordinates, use the topology of uniform convergence on compact coordinate subsets of every derivative of every local component; connection coordinates are differences from a supplied reference connection. Boundary or decay restrictions and any other completions must be declared. In these charts $C^1$ means that the directional derivative $df_x(h)=\lim_{t\to0}(f(x+th)-f(x))/t$ exists, is continuous linear in $h$, and is jointly continuous in $(x,h)$; chart transitions and their inverses are $C^1$. Tangent vectors are velocities of $C^1$ curves, identified by their chart derivatives. Require group multiplication, inversion, and the action $a:\mathcal G\times\mathcal F_{\bar0}\to\mathcal F_{\bar0}$ to be $C^1$. Put $\mathfrak g=T_e\mathcal G$ and define the infinitesimal orbit map $R_\varphi(u)=d(a(\cdot,\varphi))_e u\in T_\varphi\mathcal F_{\bar0}$. Odd fields retain their declared anticommuting coefficients; these ordinary tangent and gauge-slice conditions concern the even configuration space.

Gauge fixing supplies a $C^1$ map $f:U\to E_f$ from a declared open $U\subseteq\mathcal F_{\bar0}$ to a specified real Fréchet space, and a supplied $C^1$ submanifold $\mathcal S=f^{-1}(0)$ with $T_\varphi\mathcal S=\ker df_\varphi$. In the sign convention used here the Faddeev–Popov operator is $\mathcal M_\varphi=-df_\varphi\circ R_\varphi:\mathfrak g\to E_f$. At each $\varphi\in\mathcal S$, specify a residual zero-mode space $\mathfrak h_\varphi=\ker\mathcal M_\varphi$ and a closed complement $\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{red},\varphi}$, with $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak h_\varphi\oplus\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{red},\varphi}$. Local transversality modulo these residual modes means the required splitting $T_\varphi\mathcal F_{\bar0}=T_\varphi\mathcal S\oplus R_\varphi(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{red},\varphi})$ and that $\mathcal M_\varphi:\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{red},\varphi}\to E_f$ is a continuous linear bijection with continuous inverse. These are supplied chartwise hypotheses, not consequences of an inverse-function theorem in arbitrary Fréchet spaces; no global slice is asserted. For connection gauge action $R_Au=-D_Au$ and $f(A)=d_{A_*}^*(A-A_*)$, this convention gives $\mathcal M_A=d_{A_*}^*D_A$. A Faddeev–Popov zero mode lies in $\ker\mathcal M_\varphi$; a connection stabilizer satisfies $D_Au=0$, and residual zero modes need not all stabilize the connection. The determinant of the reduced operator requires a separately specified regularization; no infinite-dimensional determinant is supplied by differentiability alone. The package supplies that determinant prescription and a ghost complex (graded ghost, antighost, and multiplier fields with an odd BRST differential). The package also specifies its integration contour $\mathcal C$, boundary conditions, and either an actual measure or a regulator map from field configurations to regulated spaces $\mathcal F_\Lambda$ with measures $\mu_\Lambda$. If a measure is only written formally as $[D\Phi]$, this notation is not a constructed measure. Applying a $Q$-exact deformation $S_t=S+tQV$ further requires an explicit assumption or proof of $Q$-invariance of the regulated measure and contour, absence or treatment of anomalies, justified differentiation under the integral, and vanishing or controlled boundary terms. This definition supplies no such proof.

For a four-dimensional gauge model in these units, $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and a fermion field has mass dimension $3/2$; the supercharge has mass dimension $1/2$ and its spinor parameter has mass dimension $-1/2$. Every additional mass, radius, equivariant parameter, and suppressed constant must be assigned dimensions in the concrete item. No metric is asserted to admit this data, and finite-dimensional equivariant identities alone do not construct a continuum field-space measure.

items.title: Adopted rigid N=4 Yang–Mills localization background on the round four-sphere
items.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt the following Euclidean source model in the conventions stated here. Let $r>0$ have units of length and let
$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5 y_j^2=r^2\}$$
have its round metric, standard orientation, and scalar curvature $12/r^2$. In stereographic coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, $\mu=1,\dots,4$, the metric is
$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$
Use the standard spin structure and the spin connection induced by the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric. Identify the four real scalar directions $5,6,7,8$ with $\mathbb H$ in the ordered basis $(1,i,\mathbf j,i\mathbf j)$. The source's internal $SU(2)_R^L\times SU(2)_R^R$ is the two-factor cover of $SO(4)$ acting on these scalar directions by $q\mapsto u_Lqu_R^{-1}$ and fixing scalar directions $0,9$. Set $SU(2)_R:=SU(2)_R^L$, take $P_R=S^4_r\times SU(2)_R$ with zero connection, and use the selected $SU(2)_R$ generator below. The global gauge group is $G=SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$; its Lie algebra consists of anti-Hermitian $2\times2$ traceless matrices and has positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by $\kappa(-i\sigma_a/2,-i\sigma_b/2)=\delta_{ab}$. Let $\Sigma$ be the declared set of bundle-sector codes for smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundles over $S^4_r$, using the nonempty minimum-rank set code of each smooth equivariant isomorphism type. As part of the sectorwise model data, supply a set-indexed family of representative bundles $P_s\to S^4_r$ with $[P_s]=s$ for $s\in\Sigma$; each $s$ is a separate gauge sector. The family is supplied data, not a choice asserted to exist for an arbitrary declared set $\Sigma$. The sector set and any sum over it are formal model inputs, not a classification or measure construction. For a chosen sector $s$, abbreviate its supplied representative $P_s$ by $P$ and write $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$. Set $E_{\mathrm{aux}}=S^4_r\times\mathbb R^7$ with its standard Euclidean inner product and fixed global orthonormal frame $e_1,\ldots,e_7$. The auxiliary field in sector $P$ is $K=\sum_iK_i e_i$, where each $K_i$ is a smooth section of $\operatorname{ad}P$; all contractions over $i$ use this fixed fiber metric.

The matter content is the massless four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ vector multiplet: one gauge connection $A_\mu$, six real adjoint scalar fields $\Phi_A$ with $A\in\{0,5,6,7,8,9\}$, and four adjoint Weyl fermions. Equivalently, its flat-space component content is one $\mathcal N=1$ vector multiplet and three adjoint $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplets. Set the topological $\theta$-term to zero in this selected model. Use the ordinary trace $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ in the defining representation of $SU(2)$ and a positive dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$. The current N=4 model carrier uses the same global group, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, the same dimensionless coupling, and connection-normalized adjoint chiral fields, with one vector and three adjoint chiral multiplets; this is an interface match for flat-space component content and normalization. This postulate separately adopts the source’s curved $S^4$ action, curvature coupling, selected-spinor algebra, gauge fixing, contour, and formal regulator inputs; it does not identify that curved action with the supplier’s flat Minkowski superspace action. For the dimensional-reduction notation, in a local gauge trivialization define the Lie-algebra-valued components $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_\nu]$, $F_{\mu A}=D_\mu\Phi_A$, and $F_{AB}=[\Phi_A,\Phi_B]$, extended antisymmetrically to $F_{MN}$. Here $D_\mu X=\nabla_\mu^{\mathrm{LC}}X+[A_\mu,X]$ on adjoint tensor fields, with the supplied spin connection on spinor indices, and $D_A X=[\Phi_A,X]$; in the fermion term $D_\mu\Psi$ includes the spin and gauge connections. These $F_{MN}$ are Lie-algebra-valued matrices, so $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is taken in the defining representation. Use $\eta_{MN}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1)$ for $M,N=0,\dots,9$. With the seven localization auxiliaries included, the adopted classical action input is
$$S_{\mathrm{off}}=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{S^4_r}d^4x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{Tr}_2\left(\frac12\sum_{M,N}F_{MN}F^{MN}-\Psi\Gamma^M D_M\Psi+\frac{2}{r^2}\sum_A\Phi_A\Phi^A-\sum_{i=1}^7K_iK_i\right).$$
Here $\Psi$ is the adjoint ten-dimensional Majorana–Weyl fermion used to package the four-dimensional fields; after Euclidean continuation it is complex and has no independent conjugate field. The chiral gamma matrices obey $\Gamma_M\widetilde\Gamma_N+\Gamma_N\widetilde\Gamma_M=2\eta_{MN}I_{16}$, with $\widetilde\Gamma_0=-\Gamma_0$ and $\widetilde\Gamma_M=\Gamma_M$ for $M=1,\dots,9$; $\Gamma_{MN}:=\widetilde\Gamma_{[M}\Gamma_{N]}$ acts on $S^+$ and $\widetilde\Gamma_{MN}:=\Gamma_{[M}\widetilde\Gamma_{N]}$ acts on $S^-$. Brackets on two indices have weight $1/2$. The blocks are symmetric and $(\Gamma_{MN})^{\mathsf T}=-\widetilde\Gamma_{MN}$ in the source basis. A spinor bilinear $\zeta B\chi$ means $\zeta^{\mathsf T}B\chi$, with no Hermitian conjugation; the background spinors commute, while fermion components anticommute. The four sphere directions have positive metric. The term with $2/r^2$ is the conformal curvature coupling of the six scalars. The Yang–Mills coupling is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi_A]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[K_i]=[F_{MN}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $[\Psi]=\mathrm{length}^{-3/2}$.

Let $\widehat\epsilon_s=(0_8,1,0_7)^{\mathsf T}$ be the normalized sixteen-component chiral spinor in the source gamma convention, with $\Gamma_{5678}\widehat\epsilon_s=\widehat\epsilon_s$ and $\Gamma_{1234}\widehat\epsilon_s=-\widehat\epsilon_s$, and set $\widehat\epsilon_c=(2r)^{-1}\Gamma_{012}\widehat\epsilon_s$. With $\Omega(x)=1+x^2/(4r^2)$, adopt
$$\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\bigl(\widehat\epsilon_s+x^i\widetilde\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_c\bigr),\qquad \widetilde\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\left(\widehat\epsilon_c-\frac{x^i}{4r^2}\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_s\right),\quad i=1,\dots,4.$$
They solve the conformal Killing-spinor system
$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\widetilde\Gamma_\mu\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_\mu\widetilde\epsilon=-\frac{1}{4r^2}\Gamma_\mu\epsilon.$$
The normalized spinor $\widehat\epsilon_s$ and the resulting $\epsilon$ are dimensionless, while $\widehat\epsilon_c$ and $\widetilde\epsilon$ have mass dimension one. Here $Q_\epsilon$ denotes the supercharge operator of mass dimension $1/2$ selected by this normalized spinor; an infinitesimal physical transformation uses a separate odd coefficient of mass dimension $-1/2$. Accordingly, $Q_\epsilon^2$, $v^\mu\partial_\mu$, $R^Q$, and the selected generator $\omega$ have mass dimension one, and the flow parameter for $v$ has mass dimension $-1$.
After Euclidean continuation, put $\Delta_\pm=\mathbb C^2$ with the defining $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ representations $\pi_\pm$, let $V_R=\mathbb C^2$ with the defining representation $\tau$ of $SU(2)_R$, and let $V_0=\mathbb C^2$ with the trivial $SU(2)_R$ representation. Define the sixteen-dimensional complex chiral module and its smooth representation by
$$W_\epsilon=(\Delta_+\oplus\Delta_-)\otimes(V_R\oplus V_0),\qquad \rho_\epsilon(s,k)=(\pi_+(s)\oplus\pi_-(s))\otimes(\tau(k)\oplus I_{V_0}).$$
Thus $\rho_\epsilon:\operatorname{Spin}(4)\times SU(2)_R\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W_\epsilon)$ is the restriction of the continued source chiral module: each four-dimensional spin chirality occurs once with the defining $SU(2)_R^L$ doublet and once with a two-dimensional multiplicity space trivial under $SU(2)_R^L$. The spinor/R field bundle is $(\widetilde F\times_{S^4}P_R)\times_{\rho_\epsilon}W_\epsilon$ with quotient relation $[(\widetilde p,p_R)h,z]=[(\widetilde p,p_R),\rho_\epsilon(h)z]$ for $h\in\operatorname{Spin}(4)\times SU(2)_R$. In local product sections its derivative is $d\epsilon_i+(d\rho_\epsilon)_e(A^S_i,A^R_i)\epsilon_i$, where $(d\rho_\epsilon)_e$ is the differential at the identity. The spin connection in $A_i^S$ is induced by the round metric's Levi-Civita connection; because the R bundle is trivial with zero connection, the $\nabla_\mu$ in this system has zero R-connection term.
The selected spinors obey the source's same-chirality conditions, in particular $\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$, so the dilation term in the supercharge square vanishes. Their bilinear $v^\mu=\epsilon\Gamma^\mu\epsilon$ is the source-normalized infinitesimal generator of the $U(1)$ isometry rotating the $(x^1,x^2)$ and $(x^3,x^4)$ planes equally; no further rescaling of this generator is made below. The corresponding internal R-symmetry generator is the skew matrix $R^Q_{AB}=2\epsilon\widetilde\Gamma_{AB}\widetilde\epsilon$ on the six scalar indices and acts by $(\delta_R\Phi)_A=R^Q_{AB}\Phi^B$. The fermion action is $\delta_R\Psi=\tfrac14R^Q_{AB}\Gamma^{AB}\Psi$ with the source reduction metric used to raise indices. These formulas adopt the ordering in Pestun (2.9); no interchange of the two commuting background spinors is assumed. In particular the transpose identity would give $2\widetilde\epsilon\Gamma_{AB}\epsilon=-R^Q_{AB}$, so that expression is not substituted with a plus sign. The gauge connection and Faddeev--Popov ghosts are R-singlets.

In the fixed global frame $e_i$ of $E_{\mathrm{aux}}$ above, take seven smooth spinor sections $\nu_i$; equivalently, $\sum_i\nu_i\otimes e^i$ is a section of the spinor bundle tensored with $E_{\mathrm{aux}}^*$. They satisfy
$$\epsilon\Gamma_M\nu_i=0,\qquad \frac12(\epsilon\Gamma^N\epsilon)\widetilde\Gamma_{N,\alpha\beta}=\sum_{i=1}^7\nu_{i,\alpha}\nu_{i,\beta}+\epsilon_\alpha\epsilon_\beta,\qquad \nu_i\Gamma_M\nu_j=\delta_{ij}\epsilon\Gamma_M\epsilon.$$
Adopt the off-shell transformations
$$Q_\epsilon A_M=\Psi\Gamma_M\epsilon,\qquad Q_\epsilon\Psi=\frac12\Gamma^{MN}F_{MN}\epsilon+\frac12\Gamma^{\mu A}\Phi_A\nabla_\mu\epsilon+\sum_iK_i\nu_i,\qquad Q_\epsilon K_i=-\nu_i\Gamma^M D_M\Psi.$$
With $v^M=\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon$, the source writes the off-shell square as $Q_\epsilon^2=-\mathscr L^{\mathrm{cov}}_v-\delta_R-\delta_\Omega$. On adjoint scalars $\mathscr L^{\mathrm{cov}}_vX=v^\mu D_\mu X+[v^A\Phi_A,X]$; on the connection it is $(\mathscr L^{\mathrm{cov}}_vA)_\mu=v^\nu F_{\nu\mu}-D_\mu(v^A\Phi_A)$. On spinors it includes the geometric spin lift, and on the seven auxiliary components it is the exact operator in Pestun (2.30), with its auxiliary-index rotation. Thus this source operator already contains the gauge connection; it must not be added to a second gauge action. The equivalent split into a separately chosen geometric lift and a gauge transformation is specified next. The dilation parameter is $2\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. This off-shell closure is for the selected generator; it does not assert finite-auxiliary closure of the full hypermultiplet algebra.

Write $\alpha_\theta=\mathrm{Fl}_v^\theta$ for the base circle action, parameterized so $\left.\frac{d}{d\theta}\right|_{0}\alpha_\theta=v$. For every declared gauge sector $s\in\Sigma$, with supplied representative $P=P_s$, adopt as additional formal model data a smooth lift $\widehat\alpha_{\theta,P}:P\to P$ of the circle flow generated by $v$, together with compatible lifts to the spin, R, and auxiliary bundle $E_{\mathrm{aux}}$; the auxiliary lift is orthogonal and has infinitesimal index action fixed by $\Xi_{ij}$ below; each $\widehat\alpha_{\theta,P}$ is a principal-bundle automorphism covering the same base isometry. Gauge-chart background connections below are chosen invariant under this lift. This postulate assumes these sectorwise lifts as inputs; it does not prove their existence for every smooth $SU(2)$ bundle. For a field bundle with induced action $\widehat\alpha_\theta^*$, define $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}\xi=\left.\frac{d}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta=0}\widehat\alpha_\theta^*\xi$. In a local gauge frame let $\beta_{v,P}$ be the even infinitesimal vertical coefficient of this fixed lift, characterized on adjoint scalar fields by $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}X=v^\mu\partial_\mu X+[\beta_{v,P},X]$ and on connections by $\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}A=\mathcal L_v A-D_A\beta_{v,P}$. Here the unadorned $\mathcal L_v$ is the ordinary Lie derivative of a local one-form. Let $\mu_{v,A}=v^\mu A_\mu-\beta_{v,P}$; this difference is a globally defined adjoint section, equivalently the contraction of the principal connection with the chosen lifted generator in these conventions. Define $\kappa_v=\mu_{v,A}+v^A\Phi_A$ and $\phi=-\kappa_v$. With $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)X=[u,X]$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A=-D_Au$, the source operator decomposes as
$$\mathscr L_v^{\mathrm{cov}}=\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}+\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\kappa_v),\qquad Q_\epsilon^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}-\delta_R.$$
Indeed, on scalars the vertical coefficients add to $v^\mu A_\mu+v^A\Phi_A$; on a connection the right side is $\mathcal L_v A-D_A(v^\mu A_\mu+v^A\Phi_A)=\iota_vF_A-D_A(v^A\Phi_A)$. Thus no gauge contribution is counted twice. A lift-adapted local frame has $\beta_{v,P}=0$ and recovers the source's local $v^MA_M$ parameter. On spinors the spacetime spin lift is used separately from $\delta_R$. On the auxiliary bundle set
$$\Xi_{ij}=\nu_{[i}\Gamma^\mu\nabla_\mu\nu_{j]},\qquad (\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}K)_i=v^\mu\partial_\mu K_i+[\beta_{v,P},K_i]+\Xi_{ij}K_j.$$
The background $\nu_i$ are gauge singlets, so their derivative here is the supplied spin derivative; the internal derivatives vanish in this massless model. The auxiliary-index contribution in Pestun (2.30) is included in this lift and there is no further independent $R$ matrix on $K_i$. The antisymmetrization is $\nu_{[i}\Gamma^\mu\nabla_\mu\nu_{j]}=\tfrac12(\nu_i\Gamma^\mu\nabla_\mu\nu_j-\nu_j\Gamma^\mu\nabla_\mu\nu_i)$.

On each sectorwise gauge chart, with the chart label suppressed in the notation below, write $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth principal connections on $P$. For a smooth vector bundle $E$, write $\Gamma(E)=C^\infty(S^4,E)$; the Lie algebra of $\mathcal G(P)$ is $\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its pointwise Lie bracket. Use the real Fréchet chart and $C^1$ conventions of the rigid-background definition. In each sector the even physical configuration space before choosing the contour is
$$\mathcal F_{P,\mathrm{phys}}^{\bar0}=\mathcal A(P)\times\Gamma((\operatorname{ad}P)_{\mathbb C})^6\times\Gamma((\operatorname{ad}P)_{\mathbb C}\otimes(E_{\mathrm{aux}})_{\mathbb C}),$$
where the complex section spaces are regarded as real spaces and carry uniform convergence on compact coordinate subsets of every derivative. Here $(\operatorname{ad}P)_{\mathbb C}=\operatorname{ad}P\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, and likewise for $E_{\mathrm{aux}}$. The physical odd coordinates are the anticommuting coefficients of $\Psi\in\Gamma((\operatorname{ad}P)_{\mathbb C}\otimes S_\epsilon)$, where $S_\epsilon$ is the spinor/R bundle with fibre $W_\epsilon$ defined above. The connection charts are $A=A_*+a$ with tangent space $\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$; the section factors have their own section spaces as tangents. Equip $\mathcal G(P)$ with the smooth-section topology and local charts obtained from the fibrewise $SU(2)$ exponential near zero in $\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)$ and group translates. Its action on these fields is the supplied $C^1$ gauge action, with connection orbit derivative $R_Au=-D_Au$. Ghost, multiplier and finite zero-mode factors below extend this configuration space with the same section topology and the finite-dimensional topology, respectively. Choose an invariant background connection $A_*$ as fixed sectorwise data, inert under $s$ and $\delta$, and set $a=A-A_*\in\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$; this difference is a globally defined adjoint-valued one-form. The induced covariant derivative is $D_Au=du+[A,u]$ in a local trivialization, and $d_{A_*}^*$ is the formal $L^2$ adjoint of the exterior covariant derivative for the round metric and $\kappa$. For $u,w\in\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)$ define $(u,w)_P=\int_{S^4}\kappa(u,w)\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ and extend this pairing to adjoint-valued forms using the metric. The background-gauge slice is $d_{A_*}^*a=0$, and the Faddeev–Popov operator is $\mathcal M_{P,A}=d_{A_*}^*D_A:\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)\to\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Define the stabilizer algebra of the background by $\mathfrak h_P=\{u\in\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P):D_{A_*}u=0\}$. Let $L^2(P)$ be the completion of $\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)$ in $(\cdot,\cdot)_P$, set $\mathfrak h_P^\perp=\{u\in L^2(P):(u,h)_P=0\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h_P\}$, and take the smooth nonzero-mode domain to be $\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)\cap\mathfrak h_P^\perp$. Since $S^4$ is connected, evaluation at one point injects $\mathfrak h_P$ into $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, so this space of parallel sections is finite-dimensional. Since $D_{A_*}h=0$ for $h\in\mathfrak h_P$, the image of $\mathcal M_{P,A}$ is orthogonal to $\mathfrak h_P$; on the background-gauge slice, $\mathfrak h_P$ is contained in its kernel. The gauge map is $f(A,\Phi,K)=d_{A_*}^*(A-A_*)$ with target $E_f=\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)\cap\mathfrak h_P^\perp$, and its differential on a tangent connection $\dot A$ is $df_A(\dot A)=d_{A_*}^*\dot A$; hence $-df_A R_A=\mathcal M_{P,A}$. Its zero set is the supplied slice submanifold with tangent $\ker df_A$. In each gauge chart, assume the kernel is exactly $\mathfrak h_P$, the reduced tangent splitting required by the rigid-background definition holds, and $\mathcal M_{P,A}$ is a continuous linear bijection of $\Gamma(\operatorname{ad}P)\cap\mathfrak h_P^\perp$ onto itself with continuous inverse; $\det'\mathcal M_{P,A}$ denotes this restricted determinant. This chartwise invertibility, the chart cover, and the determinant are formal gauge-fixing inputs; no global gauge slice or determinant construction is asserted. In the trivial bundle with $A_*=0$, $\mathfrak h_P$ is the space of constant $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued sections and these definitions reduce to $d^*A=0$ and $d^*D_A$.

The odd ghost and antighost fields $c,\widetilde c$ and even multiplier $b$ are smooth sections of $\operatorname{ad}P$; their zero modes lie in $\mathfrak h_P$. The even zero-mode fields $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b_0$ and odd zero-mode fields $c_0,\widetilde c_0$ lie in $\mathfrak h_P$, so they need not be globally constant. Their coefficient spaces are complexified when imposing the Euclidean contours; $\mathfrak h_P$ still denotes the real parallel-section space, and the gauge action and brackets extend complex-linearly to its complexification. The lift above is assumed to fix $\mathfrak h_P$ pointwise. Assign mass dimensions $[c]=\tfrac12$, $[\widetilde c]=\tfrac32$, $[b]=[b_0]=2$, $[a_0]=[\phi]=1$, $[\widetilde a_0]=3$, $[c_0]=\tfrac52$, and $[\widetilde c_0]=\tfrac72$; here brackets denote numerical mass dimensions. Both $s$ and $\delta$ have mass dimension $1/2$. Take positive dimensionless $\xi_1,\widehat\xi_2$ and set $\xi_2=\widehat\xi_2/r^2$, of mass dimension two. With the unnormalized four-dimensional pairing $(\cdot,\cdot)_P$, each term of the following odd gauge fermion has mass dimension $-1/2$, so its $\delta$ and $Q$ variations are dimensionless. In each gauge chart, adopt the sectorwise BRST functional
$$S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]=\delta\left((\widetilde c,\,i d_{A_*}^*a+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}b+i b_0)_P-(c,\,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0)_P\right).$$
Let $\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]$ be the odd functional inside this variation. In the sectorwise gauge-fixed formulas, $\omega$ denotes the same source-normalized generator as $v=\epsilon\Gamma\epsilon$. Define
$$\delta_{U(1)}(\omega):=-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}-\delta_R,\qquad \rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega):=-\mathcal L_v^{\mathrm{lift}}\quad\text{on adjoint-valued ghosts}.$$
The second operator restricts to the stated zero-mode domains, where it vanishes by the chosen lift; the first includes the declared auxiliary-index action on $K$. The exact sectorwise completion is $S^Q_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]=Q\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]$, with $Q=s+\delta$ and $\psi=sA\in\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$ odd. In the conventions displayed here its expansion is
$$S^Q_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]=S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}[P]-(\widetilde c,\,i d_{A_*}^*\psi+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c)_P-(\phi,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0)_P.$$
In particular the factor $i$ in the first term follows from the chosen gauge fermion and $\psi=sA$. The invariant background $A_*$, the metric pairing, and the fixed zero-mode algebra make $\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}$ invariant under $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$, so the adopted algebra gives $Q S^Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q^2\Psi_{\mathrm{gf}}=0$. For nontrivial $P$, the lift, background-gauge chart, zero-mode complex and this completion are additional formal model inputs; Pestun's trivialization-chart calculation does not construct them.
The gauge-fixed functional integral is the formal expression
$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\sum_{[P]\in\Sigma}\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})} \int_{\mathcal C_P}[DA\,D\Phi\,D\Psi\,DK\,Dc\,D\widetilde c\,Db\,Da_0\,D\widetilde a_0\,Db_0\,Dc_0\,D\widetilde c_0]\, e^{-S_{\mathrm{off}}[P]-S_{\mathrm{gf}}^Q[P]}.$$
Here $D\Phi=\prod_{A\in\{0,5,6,7,8,9\}}D\Phi_A$ and $DK=\prod_{i=1}^7DK_i$. The contour $\mathcal C_P$ concerns the full independent tuple $(A,\Phi,\Psi,K,c,\widetilde c,b,a_0,\widetilde a_0,b_0,c_0,\widetilde c_0)$; odd factors denote formal Berezin integration over their anticommuting coefficients. The $c,\widetilde c,b$ factors include their own $\mathfrak h_P$ modes; the five explicitly added zero-mode variables are additional fields, each integrated once. The composite $\phi=-\kappa_v$ and the background spinors are not additional independent integration variables, and there is no independent conjugate of $\Psi$. This notation remains formal and constructs no continuum measure. In this sum the index is the sector code $s=[P]\in\Sigma$ and $P$ denotes its supplied representative $P_s$. Here $\mathcal G(P)$ is the smooth gauge-automorphism group of $P$, $\mathcal C_P$ is the declared contour in that sector, and $\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})$ is the source's formal gauge-group volume with its invariant measure scaled by the gauge coupling; it is not an actual infinite-dimensional Haar measure. In the Euclidean contour, gauge fields and $\Phi_{5},\dots,\Phi_9$ lie in the real Lie algebra, $\Phi_0=i\Phi_0^E$ with $\Phi_0^E$ real, the seven localization auxiliaries satisfy $K_i=iK_i^E$ with $K_i^E$ real, and $a_0=i a_0^E$ with $a_0^E$ real.

Use $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)$ with the infinitesimal gauge-action convention specified above, and use the combined circle/R operator $\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ and ghost action $\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)$ defined above. The supersymmetry differential acts by $sX=X'$, $sX'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X$, $sc=\phi$, $s\phi=0$, $sa_0=0$, $s\widetilde c=s\widetilde a_0=sb_0=s\widetilde c_0=sc_0=0$, and $sb=\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c$. The Faddeev–Popov differential acts on an adjoint-valued tensor field $X$ by $\delta X=-[c,X]$ and on its opposite-parity partner by $\delta X'=-[c,X']$. On the gauge connection it acts by $\delta A_\mu=D_\mu c=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(c)A_\mu$, using the earlier convention $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$; the connection's one-form superpartner $\psi$ transforms as $\delta\psi=-[c,\psi]$. The remaining rules are $\delta c=-a_0-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $\delta a_0=0$, $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]+\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$, $\delta\widetilde c=b$, $\delta b=[a_0,\widetilde c]$, $\delta\widetilde a_0=\widetilde c_0$, $\delta\widetilde c_0=[a_0,\widetilde a_0]$, $\delta b_0=c_0$, and $\delta c_0=[a_0,b_0]$. Here $X$ ranges over homogeneous adjoint-valued physical and auxiliary doublet coordinates other than the connection and the unpaired $\phi$, $X'$ has parity opposite to $X$, $c,\widetilde c,c_0,\widetilde c_0$ are odd, and $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b,b_0,\phi$ are even. The total localization differential is $Q=s+\delta$, with $s$ the supersymmetry differential and $\delta$ the Faddeev–Popov differential. These rules give, on adjoint-valued tensor fields and their superpartners,
$$s^2X'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X'+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X',\qquad \delta^2X=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)X,\qquad \{s,\delta\}X=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X,$$
and the same graded algebra on the connection and its one-form superpartner when the gauge action on the connection is interpreted as $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$. On the gauge-fixing ghosts other than the unpaired $\phi$, $\{s,\delta\}=\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)$ and $s^2=0$; the displayed ghost transformations give $\delta^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)$. Thus $Q^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ on fields and ghosts: a gauge transformation generated by the zero-mode section $a_0\in\mathfrak h_P$ plus the selected combined spacetime/R action. The affine rule for $\phi$ is important: $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]+\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$, equivalently $-[c,\phi+\omega]$ in semidirect-product notation, not $-[c+\omega,\phi]$. For example, $s\delta c=-[\phi,c]$ and $\delta sc=\delta\phi$ give $\{s,\delta\}c=\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$; together with the graded Jacobi identity this gives $Q^2c=[a_0,c]+\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)c$. This convention agrees with Pestun (4.12); the differently ordered entry printed in (4.10) is not used as an identity. These are the finite-dimensional geometric symmetry data of the background; this assertion does not identify the infinite-dimensional field space with a smooth finite-dimensional manifold.

Adopt as a formal regulator the supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative deformation used by the source for gauge-field regularization on $\mathbb R^4$. Its $\Omega$-background is the $U(1)^2$ action rotating the two coordinate planes in $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$, with angular parameters $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=r^{-1}$, each of mass dimension one. For the four-sphere, assume an extension exists and agrees near the north and south poles with the stated $\mathbb R^4$ regulator. This extension is not explicitly constructed in the source and is an additional unresolved model assumption. The regulated measure, contour, and gauge-fixed action are likewise formal inputs; any use of $S_t=S+tQV$ is conditional on measure and contour invariance, no anomalous Jacobian, justified differentiation under the integral, and no uncontrolled boundary contribution. This postulate is a source-qualified modeling choice, not a proof of a continuum path integral or a result about nature.

items.statement: Let $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_4>0$ be lengths and let $T^4_\ell=\mathbb R^4/(\ell_1\mathbb Z\oplus\cdots\oplus\ell_4\mathbb Z)$ have its quotient flat metric and standard orientation. Use $F_g^+=T^4_\ell\times SO(4)$ and $\widetilde F=T^4_\ell\times\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ with covering map $(x,s)\mapsto(x,\rho(s))$, where $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$ and $\rho(u_+,u_-)q=u_+qu_-^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$. Equip this trivial spin lift with its periodic spin structure and zero spin connection. Use the trivial $SU(2)_R$ bundle with zero connection and zero supergravity auxiliary fields. For the geometric Killing-spinor equation $\nabla^S_\mu\epsilon=0$, every constant nonzero section of $S_+$ is a solution. These data supply only the geometric spin/R and Killing-spinor input; they do not specify an off-shell multiplet or $Q$, gauge fixing, an integration contour, a measure, or a regulator, and therefore are not a complete localization package.
